common_name: Windswept Oklahoma Sunset Daylily (Red-Orange Watermarked Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, giving this vigorous tetraploid room to build a heavily branched clump.

directions: Windswept Oklahoma Sunset is a tetraploid daylily registered by Lopp from a Wispy Rays by Highland Pinched Fingers cross, bearing deep sunfast red flowers over six inches across with a contrasting orange watermark above a yellow-to-green throat. Dormant foliage sends up well-branched scapes carrying roughly twenty buds across four branches, extending the midseason-to-late bloom window considerably longer than typical daylilies. This cultivar won the AHS President's Cup in 2024 as the most outstanding daylily observed by attendees touring gardens at the National Convention. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this semi-evergreen diploid reblooms readily when kept well fed and watered.

directions: New Series is a diploid daylily bred by Kate A. Carpenter from an Arkansas Bright Eyes by Shibui Splendor cross and registered in 1982, bearing clear light pink flowers over seven inches across with a rose-red eyezone and a bright lime green throat. Its semi-evergreen foliage supports an extended midseason bloom habit and genuine rebloom through the season, with flowers classed in the extra-large show category. This cultivar won the AHS Don C. Stevens Award in 1991, recognizing it as the most outstanding eyed or banded daylily of that year. Divide crowded clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.
